comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (Phase 1 / rebar-debug, analysis only — no code changed).

## The mechanism

The only `cache_control` breakpoint rebar ever places is on the SYSTEM-prompt block (plus tool
definitions). `capabilities.cache_settings_for` (src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:333-355) sets
exactly `anthropic_cache_instructions=True` + `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True` and its
docstring states outright that "neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched".
pydantic-ai honours that by putting `cache_control` on the last system-prompt block only
(.venv/.../pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py:1578-1616) and on the last tool (ibid. 1186-1194).

For BOTH failing call sites the marked system block is tiny and the real payload rides in the
USER message, after the breakpoint, where nothing is marked:

* `coach_notes` — the `<!--volatile-->` marker sits at line 20 of the 22-line
  src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_coach.md, so `prompts.resolve_prompt_cached`
  (src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:438-465) keeps only the 9-line stance prose as the stable
  system prefix and routes `{{plan}}` into the user message.
* the haiku sub-call is `enrich()` / ticket-digest (src/rebar/llm/enrich.py:82 binds
  TRIVIAL_CLASS = claude-haiku-4-5; lines 94-98 render the prompt as `system_prompt` and pass the
  whole ticket text as `instructions`).

Anthropic SILENTLY declines to cache a breakpoint whose prefix is under the model minimum — no
error, `cache_creation=0`, `cache_read=0` — which is exactly the reported reading.

## Experiment 1 — captured outbound request (one layer below the warning)

Harness wrapped the httpx transport at the `_wrapped_transport` seam of
`anthropic_model._build_retrying_anthropic_model` (src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:95-161) and
dumped the JSON body before it left the process. Real config, real runner, real prompts:

```
COACH_NOTES  model=claude-opus-4-8 (config's default; the run used sonnet)
  system block[0]  602 chars ~150 tokens   cache_control={'type':'ephemeral','ttl':'5m'}
  tools: 0
  user message   27712 chars ~6928 tokens  cache_control=None
  markers present: ["system[0]"]

ENRICH/ticket-digest  model=claude-haiku-4-5
  system block[0] 1909 chars ~477 tokens   cache_control={'type':'ephemeral','ttl':'5m'}
  tools: 0
  user message   25304 chars ~6326 tokens  cache_control=None
  markers present: ["system[0]"]
```

## Experiment 2 — live A/B that discriminates size from the alternatives

Identical marker, identical large user message; only the marked prefix size varies
(claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5, each called twice, `cache_creation`/`cache_read` read
off `usage`):

```
haiku-4-5   marked prefix  1193 tok -> write=0     read=0        NOT CACHED
haiku-4-5   marked prefix  2748 tok -> write=0     read=0        NOT CACHED
haiku-4-5   marked prefix  4749 tok -> write=4742  read=4742     CACHED
haiku-4-5   marked prefix  7182 tok -> cached
sonnet-4-5  marked prefix   253 tok -> write=0     read=0        NOT CACHED
sonnet-4-5  marked prefix  7930 tok -> write=7923                CACHED
```

The empirical floor for both models sits between 2748 and 4749 tokens. rebar marks 150 and 477.

## Hypotheses REJECTED

* (a) "these paths never place a cache_control breakpoint" — REJECTED. The captured request shows
  `cache_control` present on `system[0]` in both cases.
* (b) "the prefix is not stable between calls" — REJECTED twice over. `cache_write=0` means no
  write was ever attempted; an unstable-but-marked prefix would still write on every call. And the
  marked block is byte-stable by construction: the coach's system prefix contains no per-run
  variable (they all sit after `<!--volatile-->`), and enrich renders its prompt with `{}`.
* "caching is unavailable / provider-side" — REJECTED: the same process cached fine for the
  Pass-1 finders, which prepend `shared_plan_prefix(plan)` into the SYSTEM prompt
  (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:282,290), producing a multi-thousand-token marked prefix.
  That is precisely the 5781-9385 cache_write rows in the report.

## On CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096

Causally involved, but not in the way the constant's docstring suggests, and it is not the cost
defect. Its VALUE is empirically about right for sonnet-4-5/haiku-4-5 (measured floor between
2748 and 4749), so calling it "the OPUS floor" understates it. The real problem is the QUANTITY it
is compared against: `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:417-422) tests
`usage["input_tokens"]` — the TOTAL billed input — when the quantity that governs whether the
cache engages is the size of the MARKED PREFIX. Both warnings are true positives, but only by
coincidence of the totals being above 4096; the same predicate applied to the marked prefix
(150 / 477) would have named the cause directly.

## Cost impact, and where a fix belongs (NOT implemented — 8415 owns llm/overlap, parity is owned
elsewhere)

* `coach_notes` is genuine, recoverable bleed: the plan is ALREADY in the Anthropic cache, written
  by the Pass-1 finders that carry it in the system prefix. The coach re-sends the same plan in the
  user message, a different slot, so it cannot hit that entry and re-pays full price every run.
* `enrich`/ticket-digest is different in kind: its 6.3k user-message payload is one ticket's text,
  unique per call, so even a message-level breakpoint would only ever WRITE, never READ. There is
  no reusable prefix at that site at all.

So the fix belongs at the SHARED seam, not the call sites. `cache_settings_for`
(capabilities.py:333-355) is the single place that decides breakpoint placement today and it
explicitly opts out of message-level caching; moving the payload back into the system prompt at
each call site would be a direct reversal of story c6e5's stable-prefix split. Two shared-seam
options worth weighing: mark the last user content block (`anthropic_cache_messages`), or use
Anthropic's automatic top-level `cache_control` (`anthropic_cache`, pydantic-ai
anthropic.py:336-346), which places the breakpoint after the whole prompt. Either one needs a
guard so a site like enrich, with no reusable prefix, does not pay write overhead for a read that
never comes.

comments.body:
PHASE 2 BLOCKED ON A DISPROOF OF THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY (rebar-debug; no code written for this
ticket). The root cause in the description is CONFIRMED and I am not disputing it. What I could
not do is implement the fix it prescribes, because the mechanism it names cannot produce a cache
READ at either site — so it would convert both calls from full price to full price + the 1.25x
write premium. Detail below so this can be re-scoped rather than re-investigated.

## The mechanism-level disproof (not an estimate — read off pydantic-ai)

Both options the description weighs place the breakpoint AFTER the entire message list:

* `anthropic_cache_messages` -> `_apply_message_cache_control`
  (.venv/.../pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py:1770-1795): "Apply per-block `cache_control` to the
  last content block of the LAST MESSAGE."
* `anthropic_cache` (automatic top-level) -> `_build_automatic_cache_control` (ibid. 1719-1736);
  Anthropic's own docs describe it as auto-caching the last cacheable block. On Bedrock/Vertex it
  degrades to `_apply_per_block_caching_fallback`, which calls the SAME
  `_apply_message_cache_control`.

So under either option the marked span ENDS with the per-call-unique tail:

* coach_notes: `resolve_prompt_cached` builds `instructions = volatile + base_instructions`
  (prompting/prompts.py:438-476). volatile is `# Plan under review` + `{{plan}}`; base_instructions
  is that run's SURVIVING FINDINGS list (plan-review.yaml:252-254). The findings differ every run,
  so the marked span is unique every run.
* enrich/ticket-digest: `instructions=source` is one ticket's text (enrich.py:96-105) — unique by
  construction, as the description already says.

A cache entry whose span always ends in unique bytes is WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. It can never
be read, on either site. The guard the description asks for would therefore have to exclude BOTH
sites, which makes the change inert rather than merely narrow.

## Why coach_notes cannot recover its cost this way even in principle

The description's premise is that the coach's plan is "ALREADY in the cache, written by the Pass-1
finders". That entry is keyed on the finders' full request prefix (render order tools -> system ->
messages), whose SYSTEM block is `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body`
(plan_review/passes.py:282,290). The coach's system block is its own 9-line stance prose. The two
requests therefore diverge at the first system byte, so no coach request — in ANY message slot —
can read the finders' entry.

Also relevant to the economics: coach_notes is a single step behind `branch: coach_gate`
(plan-review.yaml:243-254), not inside a `loop`/`map`/`batch`. It is exactly ONE call per gate run.
There is no second coach call within the 5-minute TTL to read whatever the first wrote.

## What WOULD work (proposed re-scope, not implemented)

A read requires a breakpoint placed BEFORE the volatile tail, at bytes shared with another request
in the same run. Two pieces, both larger than this ticket's stated scope:

1. `pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint` (messages.py:692; honoured at anthropic.py:1234) is the only
   mechanism that can put a breakpoint MID-message — i.e. between the reusable plan and the
   per-run findings. That is a RunRequest content-list change, which the description explicitly
   notes today's design avoids so the structured-output retry path stays untouched.
2. Even with the CachePoint, the coach needs a REUSABLE counterpart. The saving only materialises
   if the plan-bearing span is a byte-identical prefix shared with the Pass-1 finder requests and
   a breakpoint sits at that shared boundary. That is a plan-review-wide shared-prefix redesign
   (passes.py / pass1.py), not a `cache_settings_for` change.

## What DID land, on the sibling ticket

AC4 of this ticket ("`warn_if_cache_ineffective` measures the MARKED PREFIX rather than total
`input_tokens`, so the warning names the cause; a test covers a large-total / small-marked-prefix
call") is IMPLEMENTED under e3cd-ba36-41c3-4661, since it is that ticket's core change and landing
it twice would have put two mechanisms at one seam. The new warning reports the coach_notes shape
(150-token marked prefix, ~6928 unmarked) naming the marked prefix and the model's floor, covered
by tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py::
test_large_total_with_tiny_marked_prefix_warns_and_names_the_marked_prefix.

AC1/AC2/AC3 are NOT met and should be re-written against the CachePoint + shared-prefix design
above before anyone picks this up again. AC5 is operator-attested and unaffected.

## Root cause — PROVEN by captured request + live A/B, not inferred

The only `cache_control` breakpoint rebar places is on the SYSTEM-prompt block (plus tool
definitions). At both failing call sites that block is tiny and the real payload rides in the USER
message, AFTER the breakpoint, unmarked. Anthropic silently declines to cache a sub-minimum marked
prefix: no error, `cache_creation=0`, `cache_read=0`.

`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:333-355` — `cache_settings_for` sets only
`anthropic_cache_instructions` and `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions`; its own docstring states
"neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched". In pydantic-ai those flags mark only
the last system block and the last tool.

CAPTURED OUTBOUND REQUESTS (httpx transport wrapped at the `anthropic_model.py:95-161` seam, real
config/runner/prompts, body dumped before it left the process):

    coach_notes            system[0]  ~150 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6928 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0
    enrich/ticket-digest   system[0]  ~477 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6326 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0

LIVE A/B isolating prefix SIZE from every other variable — identical marker, identical large user
message, only the marked-prefix size varies:

    haiku-4-5    1193 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    2748 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    4749 tok -> w=4742 r=4742    CACHED
    sonnet-4-5    253 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    sonnet-4-5   7930 tok -> w=7923           CACHED

Empirical floor sits between 2748 and 4749 for BOTH models. rebar marks 150 and 477.

WHY THE PASS-1 FINDERS CACHE FINE in the same process: `plan_review/passes.py` returns
`shared_plan_prefix(plan) + body` for `PASS_FINDER`, putting a multi-thousand-token prefix in the
SYSTEM slot — those are the 5781-9385 cache_write rows in the same run.

Contributing detail for coach_notes: `reviewers/plan_review_coach.md:20` places `<!--volatile-->` two
lines from the end, so `resolve_prompt_cached` leaves only ~9 lines of stance prose in the system slot
and routes `{{plan}}` to the user message.

## Rejected hypotheses

* "No breakpoint is placed" — REJECTED: the captured request shows `cache_control` on `system[0]` in
  both cases.
* "The prefix is unstable between calls" — REJECTED twice: `cache_write=0` means no write was ever
  ATTEMPTED, and an unstable-but-marked prefix still writes on every call; separately the marked block
  is byte-stable by construction.
* "Provider-side caching unavailable" — REJECTED: finders cached in the same process, same provider.

## The two sites are NOT the same problem

* `coach_notes` is genuine RECOVERABLE bleed. The plan is ALREADY in the cache, written by the Pass-1
  finders that carry it in the system prefix. The coach re-sends the same plan in a different slot, so
  it cannot hit that entry and re-pays full price every run.
* `enrich`/ticket-digest is different in kind. Its ~6.3k user payload is one ticket's text, unique per
  call, so even a message-level breakpoint would only ever WRITE, never READ. There is no reusable
  prefix at that site at all — a naive fix there ADDS cost.

## A separate, sharper defect this exposed in the warning itself

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) compares total `input_tokens` against
`CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, but what actually governs caching is the MARKED PREFIX size. The two
warnings observed were true positives only by coincidence of the totals clearing 4096. The same
predicate applied to the marked prefix (150 / 477) would have named the cause directly instead of
merely flagging a symptom. Note also that 4096 is roughly right for sonnet-4-5 and haiku-4-5 too, so
the "OPUS floor" comment understates its generality.

## The obvious fix is DISPROVEN — do not retry it

The earlier remedy in this ticket (place the breakpoint at the `cache_settings_for` seam via
`anthropic_cache_messages` or `anthropic_cache`, with a guard excluding no-reusable-prefix sites) was
implemented up to the point of disproof and REJECTED on evidence:

* BOTH mechanisms mark AFTER THE ENTIRE MESSAGE LIST. `anthropic_cache_messages` routes to
  `_apply_message_cache_control`, which marks "the last content block of the LAST MESSAGE";
  `anthropic_cache` reaches the same function on the Bedrock/Vertex fallback path. So the marked span
  always ENDS with per-call-unique bytes — for `coach_notes` the run's surviving-findings list appended
  after `{{plan}}` by `resolve_prompt_cached`, for `enrich` the ticket text.
* That makes both sites WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The guard would therefore have to exclude BOTH,
  making the change inert rather than narrow.
* THE RECOVERY PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG. This ticket previously asserted `coach_notes` could hit the
  cache entry the Pass-1 finders write. It cannot: the finders' entry is keyed on a system block of
  `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body`, while the coach's system block is its own stance prose. The
  two requests diverge at the FIRST SYSTEM BYTE, so no coach request in any slot can read that entry.
* `coach_notes` is a SINGLE step behind `branch: coach_gate` — one call per gate run, not a loop. So
  even a correct breakpoint only ever reads if a PREVIOUS gate run wrote the same prefix within the
  5-minute TTL.

## What a real fix would require

A read needs a breakpoint BEFORE the volatile tail — `pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint`, which is a
`RunRequest` content-list change the current design deliberately avoids — PLUS a plan-review-wide
shared-prefix redesign so the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with the finders. Both are larger
than this ticket as originally scoped, and the second changes a precision-sensitive prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] FIRST, AND GATING THE REST: the recoverable saving is QUANTIFIED before any redesign is
      committed to. Measure what a correct breakpoint would actually recover for `coach_notes` given
      that it fires once per gate run and the cache TTL is 5 minutes — i.e. the realistic cross-run hit
      rate, not the per-call token count. `enrich`/ticket-digest is excluded from this measurement (see
      below).
- [ ] If the measured saving does NOT justify a `CachePoint` migration plus a shared-prefix redesign,
      the correct outcome is to CLOSE THIS AS WON'T-FIX with the measurement recorded. That is an
      acceptable and expected result, not a failure — the cheap fix is disproven and the expensive one
      may not earn its cost.
- [ ] `enrich`/ticket-digest is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for caching and recorded as such: its payload
      is one ticket's unique text per call, so it can only ever WRITE, never READ. Adding a breakpoint
      there would ADD cost. This is written down so a future reader does not "complete" the fix by
      including it.
- [ ] ONLY IF PROCEEDING: the breakpoint is placed BEFORE the per-call-volatile tail, and a test
      asserts the MARKED SPAN ENDS BEFORE the first per-call-unique byte. A test that merely asserts
      "a cache breakpoint exists" passes for the wrong reason — that was already true when the bug was
      filed.
- [ ] ONLY IF PROCEEDING: the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with whatever writes the entry it is
      meant to read, demonstrated by a captured request pair showing a common marked prefix — because
      without that a write is never read and the change is inert.
- [x] SATISFIED BY ticket e3cd (commit 25f5146dc0): `warn_if_cache_ineffective` now measures the MARKED
      PREFIX against that model's floor rather than total `input_tokens`, and names the cause. Do not
      re-implement this here — that is the duplicate-mechanism trap.
- [ ] ONLY IF PROCEEDING: [operator-attested] a real run after the fix shows nonzero cache_READ (not
      merely cache_write) for `coach_notes`, cited from REBAR_USAGE_LOG with run sha and timestamp. A
      write alone proves nothing here, since write-only is the defect.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
